name: OET-RV
scope: Explicit 82-book OET-RV source profile: 66 core books, 15 previously reviewed DC books, and Latin-tradition LAO with reviewed reference boundaries. Earlier reviewed mappings and unresolved intervals are retained. LAO 1:1-20 maps individually to the BOS reference; this does not claim identical textual readings.

evidence.method: RV source: Acts 19 has verses 40 and 41; 2 Corinthians 13:12 combines both greetings and 13:13 is the blessing; Philippians 1:16 selfish ambition, 1:17 love; 3 John has 15 verses; Revelation 12 has 18. OT follows standard English numbering.
evidence.attribution: OT definitions use Copenhagen Alliance data and the BOS supplement (CC BY-SA 4.0); see source-manifest.json. NT uses the reviewed VLT and BibleTagsNT boundaries.

deuterocanonicalReview.method: Native chapter maxima, missing labels and stored bridges were inventoried from all 15 local RV DC ESFM files. Copenhagen sniffing rules identify candidate differences; exceptional boundaries were checked against RV and the Greek LXX USFM witnesses. Shared numbering uses the Copenhagen org address convention; equal counts alone are not evidence for exceptional chapters. Mappings describe passage addresses, not manuscript-level textual identity. No Bible text or external runtime dependency is included.
deuterocanonicalReview.attribution: RV DC source headers credit the public-domain World English Bible British Edition (eBible.org). Copenhagen Alliance versification data is CC BY-SA 4.0, attributed in source-manifest.json and Copenhagen/LICENSE.md. This BOS address review is distributed with the profile under CC BY-SA 4.0.

referenceWitnesses.attribution: Michael Johnson, World English Bible project; public-domain source used by the RV DC files.

unresolvedRanges.TOB 13:6-10: The full reference passage around the Greek witness lacuna is not verified. The Brenton/RV correspondence alone cannot establish the missing reference boundaries. No identity fallback or assertion of absent text is made.
unresolvedRanges.ESG 1:1; 3:13; 4:17-47; 5:1-2; 8:12; 10:: Integrated additions require a reviewed reference segment convention. Ordinary intervals are explicitly mapped; no whole-book identity is declared.
unresolvedRanges.DNG 1-12: The provisional reference composite remains unresolved. Mapping these chapters to Hebrew DAN would introduce duplicate candidates within this profile. Chapters 13-14 are explicitly mapped to SUS/BEL instead.

notes: Canonical BOS codes GES, LES and DNG correspond to source filenames ES1, ES2 and DAG; existing local ESFM book-code normalization handles them.
Baruch chapter 6 maps to the separate LJE reference book; it is not an additional source book.
Stored verse bridges are recorded as source evidence, not blindly turned into semantic mergedVerses: several Sirach bridges contain only editorial omission notes.
Sirach’s prologue stays outside numbered scripture. The Greek USFM witness stores its wisdom opening at 1:1h; this is not adopted as an RV suffix.
The reference remains 1-draft. The reviewed 66-book RV mappings and pinned Copenhagen files are unchanged. LV DC mappings and partial ESG/DNG support are recorded in version 3.

partialBookReview.method: Enable only the ordinary ESG intervals specified in definition.mappedVerses and the standalone SUS/BEL bridges in DNG 13-14; reviewed against the LV Brenton source and Greek .LXX witnesses. Additions in ESG and DNG 1-12 remain unsupported by absence of any declared edge or identity fallback. See OET-LV evidence.deuterocanonicalReview for source hashes.
partialBookReview.notes: This narrows the version 2 whole-book restrictions; earlier unresolved-book notes apply only to the remaining intervals.

laodiceansReview.method: Compared the actual 20 ESFM verses, Lightfoot Latin (1875, pp. 353-355), James English (1924, pp. 478-479), and the numbered English boundary witness used by BOS reference-policy LAO. All 20 numbered passage boundaries correspond individually. This is a passage-address review, not an assertion of identical readings or approval of the draft translation.

boundaryConvention.1-14: Greeting, thanks, warning, work, bonds, salvation, living/dying, unity, obedience, God at work, action, rejoicing, requests: each passage stays within its corresponding numbered verse.
boundaryConvention.15: Complete list of qualities and instruction to do them.
boundaryConvention.16: Retain what was heard and received.
boundaryConvention.17: Peace. This is the final clause of printed Lightfoot 16, explicitly split by the OET importer.

laodiceansReview.limits: Wycliffe-Zefania 15-16 remains an atomic group when converting to/from OET. No holy-kiss greeting is substituted for verse 17. Neither a common 20-verse count nor this review certifies every Latin witness. Individual word alignment is outside this profile.
laodiceansReview.attribution: Lightfoot and James are public-domain editions. OET text is CC BY-SA 4.0. The Marlowe rendering was consulted only to compare boundaries with the existing BOS convention; no copyrighted translation text is bundled. This address review uses the profile CC-BY-SA-4.0 licence.
